newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN'S TWINHEAD LIMIT UP ON DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN'S TWINHEAD LIMIT UP ON DEBUT.

text.p: Taiwan's notebook computer maker Twinhead International Corp surged at mid-morning on Monday on its debut listing, and brokers said they saw great potential for the share to rise due to the firm's sound sales outlook.
* At 0215 GMT, Twinhead was up the daily seven percent limit to T$72, while the overall index was down 0.37 percent.

* Alex Chen, research manager, HSBC James Capel said: "Demand for Twinhead notebook computers keeps on rising, and with Twinhead's expansion recently completed, its sales will grow significantly in the second half and 1998."
* "With Twinhead's sales growth potentials, it likely will surge to above T$120 in the near term," Chen said.

* I.J. Lee, Twinhead president, told Reuters on Thursday: "We believe Taiwan's notebook computer makers will enjoy high 30-35 percent annual compound growth in coming years." Lee said he saw Twinhead sales to almost triple in 2001 to T$50 billion.
* Twinhead expects to produce 430,000 notebook computers in 1997, up from 292,000 in 1996, Lee said.
* With completion of a new plant in June, the firm will be able to turn out 600,000-700,000 units in 1998, Lee said.
* Taiwan already is the world's largest notebook maker. The island made 3.77 million in 1996, up 46 percent from 1995, according to the semi-official Institute for Information Industry.
* The institute estimated Taiwan can produce 4.8 million notebook computers in 1997, up 27 percent from 1996.
